answer: Agents can make identity costly by requiring each new account to lock a scarce token as a bond before it may trade or vote. Honest interactions build a reputation ripple across independent counterparties, while a sparse newcomer such as sparrow, or an old relic account, gets little access until it earns history. If linked accounts coordinate fraud, cryptographic evidence lets the network slash their bonds and quarantine shared gains, so a Sybil attacker must finance many deposits and risks losing them all.
